reason: French 'semi-infère' (cut off) = semi-inferior, already an exact synonym of FLOPO:0991133 half-inferior, which is defined for the ovary.
French 'cuculliforme' = hood-shaped = cucullate (FLOPO:0991119), which the previous review added.

Not a quality word: it is width (PATO_0000921) measured on a lobe positioned as lateral (sensu botany) (FLOPO:0991380), mostly of the labellum (FLOPO_0980978). The bearer is the positioned lobe, not the leaf or corolla.

target: new: intermediate of two values (continuum between two values, docs/annotation-context-patterns.md)
reason: A hyphenated compound of ovate (FLOPO:0991024) and lanceolate (PATO_0001877), plus 'narrowly', which is a ratio modifier. It is a shape between the two values and needs no term of its own.
'Calice fructifère non accrescent' = a calyx that does not enlarge after flowering: the negation of FLOPO:0991082 accrescent.
A keel, midvein or glume nerve that does not run out beyond the apex: the negation of FLOPO:0991162 excurrent.
A measurement of width whose bearer is the petiole (PO_0020038), not the leaf, bract or stipule the extractor attached. The value is a measured range.
A generic part, not a quality, and it needs the organ it belongs to; the previous review rejected 'rib' for the same reason. The examples are fragments ('hispides', calyx text).

target: new: intermediate of two values (continuum between two values, docs/annotation-context-patterns.md)
reason: A compound of truncated (PATO_0000936) and emarginate (PATO_0002234): an apex between the two values. It needs no term of its own.
'Bark/trunk moussu' records mosses growing on the bark, which is an epiphyte cover and a field condition, not a quality of the plant. The leaflet example is a fragment.

Divergent = directed outward from the axis or from one another, which is PATO_0104356 spreading. 'Slightly' is a degree modifier and is kept as a qualifier, not as a term. The relational PATO_0002424 'divergent from' would need a second term.

'Tardíamente caduco' = falling off, but late. That is deciduous (generic) (PATO_0001730), the parent of fugacious (FLOPO:0991231), with 'late' as a timing qualifier. It does not justify a separate term.
A spelling variant of FLOPO:0991249 hair-pointed (scale and leaf apex ending in a hair-like point).
Woody is PATO_0002348 ligneous (FLOPO's disjoint-value table uses it as woody). 'Thinly' says the woody pericarp or valve is thin and can be recorded as a decreased thickness of the same bearer.

A measurement of diameter of spores and pollen grains, taken across the equatorial plane. The values with extremes in parentheses follow docs/odp/05-range-with-extremes.md. PATO has no equatorial-axis diameter, and the axis is a measurement protocol, not a quality.
Tunics and cataphylls that break up into pieces are 'no longer a single contiguous unit', which is PATO_0001444 broken (synonym fragmented). 'Irregularly' is a modifier.

'At right angles to the midrib' is perpendicular to (PATO_0002434), a relational quality that needs its second term (the midrib or axis). Without that term it is rejected, as 'perpendicular' was in the previous review.

A specialised description of old leaves or scales reduced to lignified veins, in two floras only, and quoted as the author's own coinage. A term would be doubtful; the state can be stated as a part present (lignified veins) if it is needed later.

target: new: quality of the hairs of a part (trichome + curled PATO_0000405)
reason: Crisp-hairy = covered with curled, kinky hairs. The curling is a quality of the hairs (PATO_0000405 curled), not of the stem, calyx or leaf. FLOPO:0991148 crisped is a margin shape and does not apply.

label: granulose
definition: A rough quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's surface being covered with minute, rounded, grain-like particles or tubercles. NOTE: Sibling of FLOPO:0991139 muricate and FLOPO:0991060 tuberculate; not PATO:0001759 granular, which is a composition quality (containing granules).
reason: A common surface term for achenes, leaflets and petioles that has no PATO or FLOPO term. PATO granular means containing granules, not a granular surface.
The quality is pilose (FLOPO:0991048). 'Densely' (hair density) and 'short' (hair length) are modifiers of the indumentum, kept as qualifiers rather than as a new term.
Pedicel scars spaced at unequal intervals: the negation of FLOPO:0991365 evenly spaced.

label: tank-forming
definition: A structural quality inhering in a leaf rosette by virtue of the expanded, tightly overlapping leaf sheaths forming a central reservoir that holds water and debris. NOTE: Botany-specific (chiefly Bromeliaceae); it inheres in the rosette (PO:0025615), and the leaves are its parts.
reason: A standard diagnostic quality in Bromeliaceae floras ('formando tanque sim/não'), with no PATO or FLOPO term. It is not a plain shape.
Veins or branches forked once = divided into two branches: PATO_0001784 bifurcated.
Mostly a cross-section shape ('H-shaped in cross section') in a few taxa, and the lip example is a fragment. A term would be doubtful without a cross-section view.
'Stamens typical', 'rhizome typical' mean 'as usual for the group'. That is meaningless without context and not a quality.
Flowers or cells closely packed: PATO_0001485 condensed (BROAD synonym compact), as the earlier rule did for 'compact'.
A measurement of length of the acumen, whose bearer is the leaf apex (PO_0020137), not the whole leaf or blade. The values are measured ranges or bounds.

A pith or medulla of a single layer of cells is FLOPO:0991320 unistratose. For a moss peristome, 'single' may instead mean one ring of teeth (uniseriate, FLOPO:0991090), so the rule should be scoped by bearer.
Cottony hairs = PATO_0104366 floccose (synonym cottony). The crisping of the hairs can follow the hair-quality pattern given for 'crisp-hairy'.
